title: CrossAct: Crossover Replays Reveal Geometry-Conditioned Action Choice
hook: A policy can preserve endpoint success across two geometries yet still fail the action-crossover test: its own-scene action chunks work, while the same chunks reassigned to the paired scene break native task success. The direction of this scene-by-action interaction, not another aggregate leaderboard gap, reveals whether the policy changes how it acts.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal: the named Directional Action-Swap Interaction is predicted to be positive on functional-geometry pairs and absent on appearance-only pairs, a regime split not reported by the closest adjacent records. Shape (b) was viable but rejected because calling endpoint success a tacit assumption would overstate abstract-only evidence; the crossover measurement is the actual contribution.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf localizes the first strategy-level divergence induced by geometry, so an aggregate success or trajectory score cannot distinguish correct early selection of a new homotopy or relation transition from late low-level recovery after committing to the old strategy 鈥?stakes: debugging and adaptation can target the wrong component, wasting simulation and GPU budget while leaving the actual planning failure untouched.
gap_closure.how_closed: C02 supplies an independent four-cell scene-by-action crossover over exactly paired simulator scenes, and heterogeneous_decomposition repeats the crossover one native action chunk at a time to return the earliest chunk whose reassignment changes native success.

core_mechanism: CrossAct constructs paired RoboTwin 2.0 scenes (A,B) by an involution T on one task-local functional collision-geometry parameter, while holding the instruction, reset seed, robot state, material and dynamics parameters, camera transform, and terminal object transform fixed; applying T twice returns the original scene, and the compiler verifies this by serialized field equality plus collision/render asset hashes before admitting a request. Each pair is authored with two actual RoboTwin expert programs, producing executable task-local action traces e_A and e_B; the pair is eligible when replayed e_A succeeds in A and e_B succeeds in B, while the crossed replays e_A in B and e_B in A do not both satisfy the native task-success predicate. This is only a trace-relative swap-sensitivity certificate: it neither enumerates strategies nor claims that either trace or path class is globally necessary. For an evaluated policy P with deterministic decoding and fixed policy noise seed, define native chunk u_{s,k} as the exact ordered low-level end-effector target deltas and gripper commands submitted by one OpenPI pi0.5 or CLOVER controller invocation at the final RoboTwin executor interface after deterministic conversion into the simulator's fixed task frame; the logging hook at that interface supplies chunk boundaries. Record closed-loop sequences a_A and a_B, then replay both sequences open loop from the same reset in both scenes, stopping at native termination or after the stored sequence is exhausted, to form Y_ts(P), the native binary success when trace t in {A,B} is executed in scene s in {A,B}. Define the Directional Action-Swap Interaction DASI(P)=0.5[(Y_AA-Y_AB)+(Y_BB-Y_BA)]; because every scene receives both traces and every trace enters both scenes, additive scene difficulty and additive trace quality cancel, leaving a trace-by-scene interaction. To localize a consequential indexed substitution, let K={0,...,min(K_A,K_B)-1}; for each k in K save the original policy state before own-scene chunk k, replace only that numeric-index chunk with the paired scene's recorded fixed-task-frame chunk, continue with the same frozen policy, and set k_star to the earliest k whose bidirectional substitution changes at least one terminal native-success outcome, or to bottom when none does. Appearance-only controls apply the exact same rendered-mesh involution used by the functional pair while retaining A's collision mesh, mass, friction, and task state, and receive the identical four-cell replay and chunk-substitution budget. CrossAct reports DASI and k_star only on expert-eligible pairs, retains bottom and unmatched-tail mass explicitly, and reports the estimands as not estimable when eligibility is empty, alongside coverage, ordinary native success, and the appearance-control interaction; it does not feed T, expert traces, pair identity, DASI, or k_star to the policy. The empirical claim remains limited to whether the tested traces exhibit scene-specific success compatibility on these paired executable scenes; why they differ is subject to the unrepaired matched-state identifiability blocker.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 - PREMISES LEDGER
P1. RoboTwin 2.0 permits deterministic reset, collision-geometry replacement, state checkpointing, and replay of task-local end-effector actions while retaining its native success predicate; this is plausible from its simulator/data-generation role but implementation compatibility is untested - falsification target.
P2. Some task families admit involutive geometry edits with two independently executable expert programs whose own/cross replay matrix is swap-sensitive; the existence and coverage of enough such pairs is untested - falsification target.
P3. If a frozen policy changes HOW in a success-relevant, geometry-conditioned way, its own-scene traces will have higher native success than crossed traces, and the first harmful chunk substitution will occur before terminal failure; untested - falsification target.
OBSERVATION-MODEL. Geometry families and intervention ranges are preregistered before policy evaluation, expert eligibility is computed without policy outputs, every requested pair and rejection reason is logged, and claims condition on the resulting expert-eligible pair population rather than pretending it is unbiased over all geometries.
ESTIMAND. For each fixed policy P, DASI is the pair-and-reset average of the four-cell native-success interaction 0.5[(Y_AA-Y_AB)+(Y_BB-Y_BA)] over expert-eligible functional pairs; the localization estimand is the empirical distribution of k_star over seeds with successful unmodified policy rollouts, reported separately from pair coverage and from appearance-only DASI.
BLOCK 2 - NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
The naive runnable version compares P's endpoint success on scene A versus scene B and aligns the two trajectories afterward. Branch (i): it falsely assumes a between-scene success difference is separable from scene difficulty and that trajectory distance identifies a consequential action choice; CrossAct confronts both failures with the complete 2x2 scene-by-action replay, whose interaction cancels additive scene and trace effects, and with one-chunk substitutions scored by downstream native success. STANDARD-TOOL FOLLOW-UP: the 2x2 crossover is textbook experimental design, but robot action traces are post-treatment, stateful interventions whose re-execution must preserve the exact control sequence, simulator reset, coordinate frame, and closed-loop suffix; the contribution is the executable replay-and-splice instrument and its policy-level reveal, not a new factorial estimator.
BLOCK 3 - DESIGN RATIONALE
The first-divergence gap stands alone: the same replay tensor supports both the headline interaction and its chunkwise localization, so no sibling module is needed. Exhaustive grammars, path-membership proofs, switch-bit group comparisons, q permutation, generic PointMap injection, fixed affordance stages, tactile signals, TAMP, and Oracle-Graph inputs were rejected because they either recreate the upheld blockers or change the diagnostic question. FULLTEXT WARNING: fulltext_degraded is true; all literature deltas and novelty claims below are abstract-level and require later method-level verification. EDGE-CASE CONTRACT. The tested localization support is the numeric common-prefix index set K={0,...,min(K_A,K_B)-1}; k_star=bottom denotes no success-changing substitution in K, unmatched tails remain explicitly untested, and an empty expert-eligible population makes DASI and k_star not estimable rather than zero.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Select RoboTwin 2.0 families with task-local action replay and editable functional collision meshes; preregister involution T, the fixed scene fields, exact rendered-mesh appearance counterpart, native success predicate, and every requested pair before policy evaluation.
2. Instantiate A and B from the same reset seed by applying T to the registered functional collision and rendered geometry; instantiate the appearance control with the identical rendered edit but A's collision mesh and physics, and reject any request for which serialized fixed fields or T-composed-twice collision/render hashes differ from A.
3. Run the two existing or modestly scripted RoboTwin expert programs through the same final task-frame executor interface to produce e_A and e_B; replay the exact recorded commands in all four expert scene-by-action cells until native termination or sequence exhaustion and emit eligible or rejected plus four outcomes and reason.
4. For each frozen OpenPI pi0.5 and CLOVER run, fix decoder and policy-noise seeds, execute closed loop once per scene, and hook the final RoboTwin executor call to store fixed-task-frame command chunks, exact invocation boundaries, observations, and simulator checkpoints without exposing pair metadata.
5. Restore the common reset and replay each stored command sequence open loop in A and B under the same simulator-noise seed, stopping at native termination or sequence exhaustion; score Y_AA, Y_AB, Y_BA, and Y_BB and compute DASI.
6. Define K={0,...,min(K_A,K_B)-1}; for each k in K restore each own-scene checkpoint, substitute the other trace's numeric-index fixed-task-frame chunk, and resume the same frozen policy closed loop to termination; output both substituted native outcomes and k_star=min{k in K: an outcome changes}, using bottom when the set is empty and marking later unmatched chunks untested.
7. Run Steps 4-6 on the exact-rendered-edit appearance controls with the same reset seeds, decoder seeds, replays, restores, and forward-pass budget as the functional pair.
8. Run endpoint-only success comparison and numeric-index post-hoc trajectory localization on the identical own-scene records as naive baselines; neither receives additional rollouts, simulator state, or expert metadata.
9. Report per-family request and eligibility coverage, ordinary success, DASI, appearance-control DASI, the full k_star distribution including bottom/unmatched-tail mass, and pair-bootstrap summaries; if no pair is eligible, report DASI and k_star as not estimable rather than emitting numeric summaries.
10. Replicate the same frozen-policy protocol on held-out RoboTwin 2.0 object instances under ordinary rendering randomization, while keeping conclusions simulator- and family-scoped.
falsification_prediction: On expert-eligible RoboTwin 2.0 functional pairs, run frozen OpenPI pi0.5 and CLOVER with the complete four-cell replay and chunk-substitution protocol, and measure native success, DASI, and k_star. If policies make success-relevant geometry-conditioned action choices, functional-pair DASI should be more positive than appearance-only DASI and harmful substitutions should localize before terminal failure even when ordinary endpoint success is matched. The single load-bearing variable is the scene-action assignment A_swap in {own,cross}; as the non-tautological negative control, apply the identical A_swap intervention to appearance-only pairs, where collision geometry and physics are unchanged, and downstream native success should return to the own-scene baseline rather than show the functional-pair interaction. The claim is falsified if functional DASI is not distinguishable in direction from the appearance control, if the interaction is explained by replay instability on the controls, or if chunk substitution never changes downstream native success.
compute_budget: 24 GPU-days on 80GB-class A100 GPUs for frozen OpenPI pi0.5 and CLOVER rollouts, four-cell replays, chunk substitutions, controls, and held-out rendering; comfortable on 4xA100 within one paper cycle. $0 paid API because RoboTwin 2.0, SAPIEN, OpenPI pi0.5, CLOVER, replay, and scoring use released code/checkpoints or local simulation.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: RoboTwin 2.0 randomizes environments and synthesizes expert code, whereas CrossAct constructs expert-qualified involutive geometry pairs and measures a four-cell scene-by-action replay interaction plus first-sensitive-chunk localization; abstract-only inference because full text was unavailable.

GemBench evaluates placement, object, primitive, and long-horizon generalization, while CrossAct cross-replays each policy's actually emitted action sequence in both matched geometries to isolate action-geometry compatibility; abstract-only inference.

CoA-VLA supplies a fixed chain of object, grasp, spatial, and movement affordances, whereas CrossAct uses no phase scaffold and identifies the first success-consequential policy chunk by simulator intervention; abstract-only inference.

CLOVER replans from visual prediction error, whereas CrossAct holds the policy fixed and measures whether geometry-specific emitted actions survive counterfactual reassignment across paired scenes; abstract-only inference.

Any3D-VLA fuses diverse point-cloud sources for spatial robustness, whereas CrossAct adds no 3D policy input and instead measures the causal downstream effect of reassigning identical action chunks between functional and appearance-controlled scene pairs; abstract-only inference.

what_step_was_missed: It would have needed to turn its simulator randomization and expert-code pipeline into involutive same-goal geometry pairs, execute both expert and policy traces in the full 2x2 scene-by-action crossover, and intervene on individual native action chunks to localize the first downstream-success divergence; this is an abstract-only inference because its method text was unavailable.
